name: 6327-fixedlength-granite20b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams = 16, warmup 20% and cooldown 10% by completion, bounded at 1024 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, so ~717 are scored.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets and no shared prefix. FIXED 128 prompt tokens / 128 output tokens (min = max on both), static seed 6327, streaming ON (ITL and TTFT are undefined without per-token timestamps), n=1, no logprobs, no structured outputs, sampling at the engine's defaults. `request_format: plain` -- this checkpoint is a base code model with no chat template, so no template is applied and the wire length is 128 plus the tokenizer's BOS. The backend sets `ignore_eos=True` whenever `max_tokens` is set, so every request generates exactly 128 tokens and nothing ends early.
purpose: A 20-billion-parameter code completion service streaming fixed 128-token replies to 16 concurrent developers on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine command line for commit a921e863921721ecae8250e0543aba1920c7c53a. Every value here is
# either declared or the engine's own default at this commit, written out so it cannot drift.
# The interpreter and hardware seal live in configs/env.yaml and are NOT portable.

model: ibm-granite/granite-20b-code-base-8k
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# The public checkpoint is bf16, so FP8 is computed at LOAD TIME (per-tensor weights, dynamic
# per-activation scales). The bf16 weights are materialised before conversion, so the high-water
# mark is ~40 GB against a ~20 GB resident footprint -- size any change to the settings below
# against that peak, not against the steady state.
quantization: fp8
dtype: bfloat16
max-num-seqs: 256
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enforce-eager: false
enable-prefix-caching: false
